articles.title: ‘Like a drill going into my eye’: why the mystery over Havana syndrome refuses to die
articles.description:
Dozens of CIA officers have been afflicted by debilitating symptoms over the past decade. Are they the result of ‘mass hysteria’? Or are they from attacks with an energy weapon and, if so, who is responsible? And has there been a cover-up?
Shortly after 1am one night in April 2019, a CIA officer on a work trip to London was jolted awake in his hotel room by the most intense head pain he had ever experienced. His body was soaked with sweat and he felt like his eyes were spinning in their sockets. He manoeuvred his way out of bed, hoping to make it to the bathroom to vomit, but found his sense of balance had deserted him. Eventually, he fell back into a fitful, shallow sleep.
The next day, arriving at the work meeting he had travelled for, the officer found he could not remember the names of colleagues in the room, people he knew well. As the meeting got under way, he could barely follow the discussion. Initially, he chalked it up to a terrible – if rather odd – case of food poisoning. But over subsequent weeks, worrying symptoms persisted: brain fog, loss of balance and increasingly harsh tinnitus.

articles.title: AI boom and trade resilience to Middle East crisis lift outlook, but gains to be uneven
articles.description: Global trade proved more resilient than expected in the first half of 2026 despite the disruption caused by the Middle East conflict, as supply chains adapted and strong investment in artificial intelligence provided a powerful boost to goods trade. However, the resilience was not uniform, with services trade and some regions more exposed to the effects of the conflict. WTO economists have therefore raised the forecast for merchandise trade growth in 2026 while lowering the outlook for services trade.
articles.titleJa: AIブームと中東危機への貿易の回復力が経済見通しを押し上げるが、その恩恵は不均一

articles.title: General Council addresses WTO reform, ministerial follow-ups, ongoing negotiations
articles.description: WTO members meeting at the General Council on 5-6 October addressed issues related to the ongoing discussions on WTO reform, follow-up to outcomes of past ministerial conferences, and the state of ongoing negotiations on various topics. Members also discussed issues related to the Agreement on Electronic Commerce, emerging agricultural trade issues, and optimizing the outcome of future ministerial conferences, among other issues.
articles.titleJa: 一般理事会、WTO改革、閣僚会議のフォローアップ、進行中の交渉について議論

articles.title: Co-sponsors of sustainability initiative advance work plan towards MC15
articles.description: At a meeting on 2 October, co-sponsors of the Trade and Environmental Sustainability Structured Discussions (TESSD) discussed a work plan for 2026-27 in preparation for the 15th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC15). They identified priorities, working methods and potential deliverables for each work area, and expressed broad support for a transition towards more flexible and outcome-oriented work.
articles.titleJa: 持続可能性イニシアチブの共同提案者がMC15に向けた作業計画を推進

articles.title: WTO MSME Group explores IP's role in trade, hears success stories and updates
articles.description: The Informal Working Group on Micro, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs) met on 2 October, with a focus on the practical role of intellectual property (IP) in helping small businesses innovate, grow and reach international markets. The meeting included an information session on IP tools and thematic presentations from members, international organizations and stakeholders. Several members reported on MSME initiatives in formal WTO committees.
articles.titleJa: WTO MSMEグループ、貿易におけるIPの役割を探求し、成功事例と最新情報を聴取

articles.title: DDG Nordquist: Trade continues apace, showing resiliency

articles.titleJa: ノルドクイスト事務次長補：貿易は活発に続き、回復力を示している

articles.title: Director-General cites concerns with pace of negotiations as chairs report on state of play
articles.description: A meeting of the Trade Negotiations Committee (TNC) on 1 October provided WTO members with an opportunity to take stock of the WTO's negotiating agenda six months after the 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) in Yaoundé and voice their views on how to advance their work. Members heard readouts from the chairs of the negotiating bodies about the state of play in their respective talks.

articles.title: Co-sponsors of Plastics Dialogue hold first round of technical discussions following MC14
articles.description: At a meeting on 1 October 2026, WTO members participating in the Dialogue on Plastics Pollution and Environmentally Sustainable Plastics Trade (DPP) held the first substantive round of discussions across four areas of work: circular solutions to plastics pollution; waste-management technologies; single-use plastics; and trade-related plastics measures. Building on the DPP's outcomes from the 14th Ministerial Conference (MC14) in March 2026 and earlier technical work, the discussions were aimed at moving towards more focused and practical work in the lead-up to MC15.
articles.titleJa: プラスチック対話の共同提案者、MC14後初の技術的議論を開催

articles.title: Members take stock of latest discussions on WTO reform
articles.description: At a transparency session on 30 September, facilitators for the discussions on WTO reform reported on recent meetings among members on the four tracks of reform: foundational issues, decision- making, development and level playing field. The facilitators noted a high level of engagement with members' written and oral proposals submitted in recent weeks. They acknowledged that momentum is building across all four tracks, but substantial work remains.

articles.title: John H. Jackson Moot Court Competition kicks off with webinar support on offer

articles.title: WTO members deepen discussions on trade and climate measures, share updates
articles.description: The Committee on Trade and Environment (CTE) met on 28-29 September to advance its discussions on the trade and environment nexus, focusing on interoperability and development aspects of trade-related climate measures. Members also built on the voluntary information sharing exercise launched earlier this year with a view to enhancing transparency of trade and climate measures in the Committee. In addition, they were briefed on work undertaken in other international fora and on developments in several member-led environmental initiatives at the WTO.
articles.titleJa: WTO加盟国、貿易と気候変動対策に関する議論を深化、最新情報を共有
